messages:
sam (Acme): Hey — we rotated our public API key ~10:12 UTC and since then ~10% of requests from our EU region return 403. Happens across a few pods/services. No deploy besides a k8s secret update.

maria (Support): Thanks — can you paste one failing request header (x-request-id) and the last 6 chars of the rotated key? Also did you rotate via Vault CLI/API or the Console?

sam (Acme): x-request-id: eu-req-8f3c91
last6: f4a9d2
Rotated with vault kv put secret/acme/api_key value=<new> then updated k8s secret and patched deployment to trigger rollout (kubectl -n acme rollout restart deploy/web). No errors during rollout.

jonathan (SRE): Two quick possibilities: 1) some long-running processes still have the old env (PID not restarted by rollout), 2) an edge/proxy cache or auth middleware cached validation results. Can you run on two different pods: `kubectl -n acme exec -it web-<podA> -- printenv | grep ACME_API_KEY` and the same for podB? Also `kubectl get rs -n acme -o wide` so we see which pods came up when.

sam (Acme): Ran checks, weird results — pod web-0 and web-2 have ACME_API_KEY matching the new key, web-1 still prints the old key. rollout status showed all pods Ready.

vault-agent-bot: vault-agent: reloaded secret lease for secret/data/acme/api_key (version 3) at 2026-02-27T10:12:30Z

maria (Support): That matches a partial rollout / env reload gap. If you updated k8s secret but some containers kept an in-memory copy of the old key (no full process restart), you'll see intermittent 403s until the pod is fully replaced. Two mitigations: a) force-delete the offending pod `kubectl -n acme delete pod web-1` to force a fresh pod, or b) if your app supports SIGHUP reload, trigger it across pods. Which do you prefer?

sam (Acme): We prefer minimal disruption. Is there a way to avoid immediate 403s while we rotate? We're getting client alerts.

olivia (Platform): Temporary allowlist would help (cut risk window) but not ideal for security. We can also purge cached auth state for that key in the edge layer. Maria — can support side do a cache purge for key suffix `f4a9d2`? If Redwood has a cached validation TTL, purging forces revalidation.

maria (Support): I can trigger an admin cache invalidation for that key prefix. Note: this invalidation is best-effort and will make the edge revalidate against the auth backend immediately. Before I do it, please confirm: the new key is already active in Vault and your k8s secrets? Also provide the service id (acct/acme-prod).

sam (Acme): Confirmed: vault kv show secret/data/acme/api_key -> version 3 is the new key. k8s secret acme-api -> key: api_key updated 10:13 UTC. Service id: acct/acme-prod.

maria (Support): Doing admin cache purge now for service acct/acme-prod and suffix f4a9d2 — will post when done.

(maria performs admin action)

maria (Support): Done — purge issued at 10:28:14 UTC. Edge nodes should revalidate; give it ~30s and retry a failing request.

sam (Acme): Retried eu-req-8f3c91 path — still 403, new x-req-id: eu-req-9b2d77. But overall 403 rate dropped from 10% to ~1.5%.

jonathan (SRE): That drop is consistent with getting most pods fresh but one stale pod. I'd still recommend deleting web-1 to force a clean process start so the in-memory env is replaced. That will stop the remaining errors.

sam (Acme): OK doing `kubectl -n acme delete pod web-1` now.

sam (Acme): Confirmed — pod gone, new pod web-4 created and shows new key in `printenv`. Observing traffic now: 403s dropped to 0.2% then disappeared.

sam (Acme): Quick postmortem note for our infra: vault-agent reported lease reload but the app wasn't configured to reload env on secret rotation — will add a small sidecar watch + exec SIGHUP to avoid manual pod deletes next time.

olivia (Platform): Good plan. Couple tips: 1) If you use Vault KV v2, ensure your sync path and versioning are consistent (some teams accidentally wrote to a new path and left an old copy), 2) consider a short grace window/allowlist during rotation windows, 3) if you rely on long-lived processes, add an automated post-rotate rollout or use a process manager that picks up env changes.

maria (Support): Glad to hear traffic normalized. If you want, we can run a quick audit of any remaining API keys for acct/acme-prod and do an on-record revoke of the old key to avoid confusion. Otherwise I'll close the ticket in 24h if no regressions. :white_check_mark:

sam (Acme): Please do the audit and revoke the old key (we'll update our client caches tomorrow). Thanks everyone — great response time. :rocket:
